findings.F1: On Sunday's last bar, the coin's 48-hour weekend return is reversed over the next 48 hours only when the weekend's volume was thin against the coin's own usual weekend-to-weekday ratio. In the thinnest third of weekends (weekend/weekday volume 0.35 on average), the winsorised slope of the 48-hour future z on the past z is -0.27 (t -4.1, 636 cases). The middle third gives -0.07 (t -1.1) and the thickest third +0.07 (t 1.6).
findings.F2: The thinness grades the reversal continuously. In a regression of the Sunday 48-hour future z on the weekend move, log volume ratio and their product, the move's slope is -0.113 (t -3.1) and the product is +0.129 (t 4.7, about 1,900 cases). The thinner the weekend, the stronger the reversal.
findings.F3: The thin-weekend reversal is broad across coins and years. In the thin third, slopes are -0.32 to -0.48 for BTC, ETH, LTC and XRP (t -2.0 to -2.8), ZEC is -0.32 (t -1.4) and XMR is -0.01. Slopes are negative in 7 of 8 years (2023 is +0.13). Betting against the move gives +0.68 % above drift per case over 48 hours (t 2.7, 636 cases), which is 3.6 times the 0.19 % trade cost.
findings.F4: Moves of the same thinness made during the week are not reversed in the same way. In the thinnest third of each weekday, the 48-hour slopes are -0.01 to -0.10 (all |t| < 1.9), against -0.27 (t -4.1) on Sunday. This fits the brief's own discrimination test.
findings.F5: The tested forecast did not capture this. All Sunday cases pooled give a slope of -0.019 (t -0.6, 2,028 cases), and the tested forecast's unusual move was -0.29 % per case (t -0.19). Its form (move times the raw weekday/weekend ratio, standardised over 500 hourly bars) does not isolate the thin-weekend cases where the reversal sits.
findings.F6: Midweek moves made on heavy volume tend to continue rather than reverse. On the 23:00 bars of Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, the 48-hour slopes in the thickest volume third are +0.079 (t 2.6), +0.081 (t 3.0) and +0.053 (t 2.0), about 615 cases each. The thin thirds on the same days give -0.03 to -0.05 (t > -1.4). This is weaker evidence given the 21 cells examined.
findings.F7: Hours 20:00 and 21:00 UTC carry a positive drift, with hourly return z +0.053 (t 6.9) and +0.043 (t 5.9) out of 24 hours examined. It holds in every coin (t 3.0 to 4.4), every weekday (t 2.4 to 4.0) and 7 of 8 years (2022 is -0.02). Its size is only about 0.04–0.05 % per hour, so the two hours together give about 0.1 %, half the 0.19 % trade cost.

ideas.idea: The thinner a coin's weekend volume is relative to its own usual weekend-to-weekday volume ratio, the larger the share of its Saturday-Sunday 2-day return that is reversed over the next 2 days. A weekend of ordinary or heavy volume sees its move continued slightly.
ideas.consequence: A trader leans against the weekend's move at Sunday's close in proportion to how unusually thin that weekend was for the coin, and stays aside or with the move when the weekend traded normally.
ideas.name: unusually thin weekend reverses

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's volume over the last 2 days is relative to its volume over the previous 5 days, in the middle and end of the week, the more its 2-day return continues in the same direction over the next 2 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader follows heavy-volume midweek moves rather than fading them, and gives them more weight the heavier the volume.
ideas.name: heavy-volume midweek moves continue
